citation.title: DL-Scale: Deep Learning for model upgrading in topology optimization
citation.authors: Nikos Ath. Kallioras, Nikos D. Lagaros
citation.version_coded: Abstract only, from OpenAlex metadata (abstract_inverted_index for https://doi.org/10.1016/j.promfg.2020.02.273); the version of record could not be read. OpenAlex marks the article 'diamond' open access with its only location at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S235197892030860X/pdf and 'any_repository_has_fulltext: false' (no mirror elsewhere). That ScienceDirect URL returned HTTP 403 to a generic-UA curl request, and inspection of the returned page showed the words 'Captcha'/'captcha' -- a bot check, not a paywall notice -- so it was not attempted further; the abstract HTML page at the same pii also returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. No arXiv version exists for this article.

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Per the abstract only: a Deep Belief Network (DBN), trained once on a reference SIMP topology-optimization problem, is combined with SIMP in an iterative 'model-upgrading' scheme that replaces one fine-mesh run with a sequence of coarser sub-problems of identical loads/supports. The abstract claims only qualitatively, across all test cases, that the computational load and the number of SIMP iterations needed on the dense mesh are 'vastly reduced'; no numeric factor, timing, or iteration count is given.
claim.key_phrase: iterations that SIMP needs to perform on a dense meshed model are vastly reduced
claim.location: abstract (read via OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index; full text not accessible)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The abstract gives no numeric speed-up factor, runtime, or iteration count; the claim ('vastly reduced' computational load and iterations) is stated only qualitatively.
claim.alternatives: none stated beyond the single general qualitative claim; the abstract gives no other candidate outcome

baseline.classical_method: SIMP (Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization) run directly on the dense/fine mesh without model-upgrading -- the implicit comparator against which 'vastly reduced' iterations are claimed [inferred from abstract wording]
baseline.problem_size: not stated (abstract mentions only 'fine discretized meshes' and 'several known to literature problems', with no sizes given)
baseline.training_time: not stated (abstract states the DBN 'is trained once on a typical topology optimization reference problem', with no cost given)

notes: No author named Jun Wang (authors: Nikos Ath. Kallioras, Nikos D. Lagaros, both National Technical University of Athens). Duplicate check: audit/pool/pool.csv has exactly one row for this exact title/DOI (P00712); no arXiv or repeated copy of this specific article exists in the pool, so FT-DUPLICATE does not apply. Note for the verifier: the pool separately contains a closely related, but textually distinct, publication by the same two authors -- P00665, 'DL-SCALE: a novel deep learning-based model order upscaling scheme for solving topology optimization problems' (Neural Computing and Applications, doi 10.1007/s00521-020-05480-8, 2020-11-10) -- which reads as an extended journal version of this conference paper (same DL-SCALE method/acronym, same author order, ~8 months later). This is not coded as FT-DUPLICATE here because it is a separate pool pid outside this queue with its own DOI and (presumably) expanded content, matching how the pool itself already distinguishes the two; a reviewer with access to both full texts should confirm whether the journal version simply reports the same experiments in more detail or adds new ones. Access: exhausted the routes available -- the DOI's only known host (ScienceDirect) returned a CAPTCHA/bot-check page (HTTP 403) to both a direct request and WebFetch, and OpenAlex confirms no alternate repository holds the full text; Procedia Manufacturing articles are not typically mirrored outside ScienceDirect. ResearchGate hosts a copy but was not used (excluded access route per task rules). Per the task's abstract-only rule, the record is coded include, stratum 'none', with all rule verdicts na, rather than excluded. Key uncertainty for a coder with full-text access: whether the fine-mesh SIMP baseline and the DL-Scale/DBN pipeline are compared at matched design quality (R1) and whether the DBN's one-time training cost is amortised or reported at all (R3) -- none of this is visible from the abstract. dim was left 'unclear' because the abstract does not state 2D/3D or problem size for any test case.
